letter.subject: Concern regarding cookie and tracking practices on lseg.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive audit of https://lseg.com on 2026-11-08 04:08 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit loaded the site, clicked the cookie banner’s “Reject all” option, then recorded what cookies were set and what requests were still sent while browsing the site.

The audit reviewed https://www.lseg.com/en/data-analytics, https://www.lseg.com/ja and https://www.lseg.com/en/ftse-russell, and also reviewed your privacy statement at https://www.lseg.com/en/policies/privacy-statement.

Please explain the following points.

1. Before any choice was made on the cookie banner, a Twitter cookie, __cf_bm, was already set. The audit recorded this as an advertising cookie, and it appeared to contain a unique identifier.

2. Before any choice was made on the cookie banner, an Adobe cookie, AMCV_3E1F57795B977DEB0A495EEA%40AdobeOrg, was already set. The audit recorded this as an analytics cookie, and it appeared to contain a unique identifier.

3. After “Reject all” was clicked, Adobe still received data. The audit recorded 36 requests to adobedtm.com after rejection.

4. Your privacy statement names 0 companies, but the audit observed Adobe and Twitter. The policy may describe recipients only by category, but our concern is that these companies were not expressly named.

5. Our review suggests that, after the visitor selected “Reject all”, the Adobe identifier cookie remained present and Adobe continued making requests. This appears inconsistent with the statement in your policy that “The preference centre available through Cookie Settings allows you to enable or disable cookies that are not strictly necessary.”

Please therefore:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking operating without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

ai_review.summary: The audit shows substantial pre-consent and post-rejection activity, including Twitter advertising activity and Adobe analytics activity, which is addressed in the automated checks. The additional finding here is that Adobe tracking appears inconsistent with LSEG’s stated ability to disable non-essential cookies. The privacy statement and cookie statement cover most core UK GDPR information areas, although the audit evidence indicates that actual cookie behaviour may not reflect the stated controls.
